Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Fast-path check surfaced Gabon's Cybersecurity Law (Law No. 027/2023), so the row was escalated to full verification. Articles 22, 27 and 36 of this law require electronic communications network operators to maintain an operational data-management centre on national territory, to host confidential/sensitive data exclusively within Gabon (absent written derogation) and to keep a copy of their data in-country. This is a sectoral (telecoms/electronic communications) requirement rather than an economy-wide data localisation regime. Value Code revised from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Sectoral requirements only).
revised_comments: Gabon's Law No. 027/2023 of 11 July 2023 on cybersecurity and cybercrime imposes sectoral data localisation obligations on electronic communications network operators. Article 22 requires operators to maintain an operational infrastructure and data management centre on national territory; Article 27 requires confidential or sensitive data to be hosted exclusively within Gabon unless the competent administrative authority grants a written exemption; and Article 36 requires every operator to retain a copy of its data domestically. These provisions apply specifically to the telecoms/electronic communications sector, while personal data generally remains governed separately by the Personal Data Protection Act (Law 001/2011, as amended in 2023).

Fresh reporting confirms that ST Digital (a Cameroon-based operator) opened Gabon's first Tier III-certified data centre in the Nkok Special Economic Zone on 3 July 2026, inaugurated by President Oligui Nguema, comprising cloud, colocation and private-suite space. revised_comments: Gabon now hosts a commercial-grade data centre. ST Digital, a Cameroon-headquartered operator, opened a Tier III-certified facility in the Nkok Special Economic Zone near Libreville on 3 July 2026, following groundbreaking in August 2025. The roughly 3,000 sqm site (an approximately US$14 million/8 billion CFA franc investment) includes dedicated cloud, colocation and private-suite halls with capacity for around 3,000 physical servers, and is staffed entirely by Gabonese technical personnel. The facility was inaugurated by President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema alongside a partnership agreement between ST Digital and the Ministry of Digital Economy.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.

revision_notes: Fast-path check surfaced substantive material, so the row was escalated to full verification. Evidence is mixed: Tracxn tracks 172 companies in Gabon with only 16 having raised disclosed funding (cumulative $175M, but just $755K in 2025 to October), and Africa: The Big Deal/UNCDF describe Gabon as a 'Tier 3' market that has not yet attracted sustained investor attention. Against this, AfriLabs lists three active hubs/incubators (Akewa Accélérateur, Société d'Incubation Numérique du Gabon, Ogooué Labs) and a functioning angel network (GAIN/Angels Gabon). This sits at the boundary between Value Code 2 (Emerging: some startups, limited funding, 1-2 hubs) and 3 (Developing: growing base, several hubs, regular funding) — annual VC funding is far below the $50m Established threshold but the hub count exceeds the Emerging band. Flagged for human review rather than asserting a single code.
revised_comments: Gabon's tech startup ecosystem remains at an early stage of development. Tracxn records around 172 startups in the country, of which 16 have raised disclosed funding (a cumulative $175 million), with only around $755,000 raised in a single round in 2025 to October. Africa: The Big Deal and UNCDF describe Gabon as a 'Tier 3' market that has so far attracted limited sustained venture capital interest compared with the continent's larger hubs. The ecosystem is nonetheless supported by three identified hubs and incubators (Akewa Accélérateur, Société d'Incubation Numérique du Gabon, and Ogooué Labs) and an active angel investor network (Gabon Angel Investor Network/Angels Gabon), alongside emerging fintech players such as CLIKPAY.

At least three public institutions offer relevant tertiary ICT/STEM programmes: Université Numérique du Gabon (licences and masters in computer science, cybersecurity, big data, AI, DevOps and data engineering), Université des Sciences et Techniques de Masuku/USTM (an established engineering and science institution since 1986, including a computer/telecommunications engineering programme), and Université Omar Bongo. revised_comments: Gabon has several tertiary institutions offering ICT and STEM programmes. The Université Numérique du Gabon (UNG), a public distance-learning institution, offers licence and master's degrees in computer science, cybersecurity, big data, artificial intelligence, DevOps and data engineering. The Université des Sciences et Techniques de Masuku (USTM), established in 1986 and incorporating the former École Polytechnique de Masuku, delivers science and engineering qualifications from technician to doctoral level, including computer and telecommunications engineering. The Université Omar Bongo, the country's oldest university, and technical training bodies such as the African Institute of Informatics (IAI) complete the landscape. Enrolment and curricula are actively growing, supported by initiatives such as the UNESCO-China Funds-in-Trust (CFIT III) programme and a 2025 workshop to embed UNESCO Global Skills Academy digital-skills certifications into university curricula.
